## How it works

- [statement] When KV cache size exceeds available headroom during extended context ingestion, Ollama dynamically reallocates context buffers, incurring allocation stalls unless context size is pinned via num_ctx in Modelfile. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.md · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/gguf.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Gemma4-12B quantized at 4-bit occupies ~7.8 GB VRAM, leaving 8.2 GB headroom in a 16GB VRAM pool for up to 32k token KV cache and activation workspaces. (high confidence) — https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad
- [statement] When running completely resident in RTX 5080 GDDR7 VRAM (~1000 GB/s), Gemma4-12B generates ~85-92 tokens per second, roughly double the ~42-45 tokens per second achieved on Apple Silicon M5 Max (~400 GB/s). (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples
- [statement] Qwen3.6-35B in 4-bit quantized representation requires ~21.9 GB base weight footprint, fitting comfortably in 64GB Unified Memory while exceeding the 16GB capacity of consumer discrete GPUs. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples/tree/main/llms · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://huggingface.co/Qwen
- [statement] On Apple M5 Max (400 GB/s bandwidth), memory-bound token generation for 35B 4-bit weights achieves 15.5 to 17.2 tokens per second, closely tracking theoretical memory bus saturation (400 GB/s / 22 GB = ~18.1 tps max). (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples/tree/main/llms · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx
- [statement] Expanding context length to 64k tokens adds ~9.0 GB to the KV cache in 16-bit float, requiring explicit dynamic context cache management or 8-bit quantized KV cache to maintain resident headroom. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples/tree/main/llms · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://huggingface.co/Qwen
- [statement] Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) heads in Qwen3.6 allow speculative verification of subsequent tokens, improving generation throughput by 20-30% on high-bandwidth memory architectures. (high confidence) — https://huggingface.co/Qwen · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Discrete eGPU GDDR7 achieves ~1000 GB/s memory bandwidth, delivering over 2x the memory-bound token generation throughput of Apple Silicon unified memory for models that fit within its 16GB VRAM limit. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/unified_memory_architecture

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Serving Gemma4-12B via Ollama Metal introduces a 10-15% throughput penalty compared to native MLX-LM due to runtime translation and generic Metal kernel dispatch in ggml. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch
- [statement] Thunderbolt 5 eGPU links provide approximately 7.0 GB/s practical unidirectional bandwidth, creating a severe bottleneck if model weights are streamed from host RAM rather than fully resident in GDDR7 VRAM. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Pre-allocation of static tensor workspaces in Tinygrad or TensorRT avoids CUDA and Metal memory fragmentation during extended generation passes. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch

(high confidence) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/main/docs/src/usage/benchmarks.rst
- [statement] Measuring peak VRAM consumption requires tracking resident set size (RSS), active Metal wired memory allocations, and discrete GPU allocated VRAM during maximum prompt length ingestion. - [statement] Reporting mean tokens per second without measuring inter-token latency variance masks stutter caused by periodic garbage collection, dynamic KV cache reallocation, and memory compaction. - [statement] Apple Silicon Unified Memory provides a shared address space allowing CPU and Metal GPU to operate on identical memory pointers without PCIe serialization or host-device DMA copies. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/unified_memory_architecture
- [statement] GGUF format structures model weights into contiguous tensor buffers aligned to 32-byte boundaries, enabling zero-copy mmap() loading directly into virtual memory pages. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/gguf.md · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.md
- [statement] On Apple Silicon macOS, Ollama orchestrates llama-server instances allocating shared Metal command buffers, mapping unified memory buffers without host-to-device PCIe serialization. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.md · keywords: Local Model Performance Evaluation: Ollama, MLX, and Hardware Architectures · also: https://developer.apple.com/metal/
